### Viz 1

::: {.callout-note title="Research Question"}

How many anti-LGBTQ bills were there on the ballot per state in 2026?

:::

```{r}
bills_by_state <- legislation_data %>%
  rename(state = State) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(bill_count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(bill_count))
ggplot(bills_by_state, aes(x = reorder(state, bill_count), y = bill_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1f78b4") +
  geom_text(aes(label = bill_count), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Anti-LGBTQ+ Bills Tracked by State",
    subtitle = "Source: ACLU Legislative Tracker",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Bills"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


::: {.callout-note title="Summary"}

Could be separated by which ones have been passed and which ones haven't, maybe make it top 10 states instead of all.

:::

### Viz 2

::: {.callout-note title="Research Question"}

What are the top 10 states with the most anti-LGBTQ legislation on the ballot in 2026?

:::

```{r}
bills_by_state <- legislation_data %>%
  rename(state = State) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(bill_count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(bill_count))  %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)
ggplot(bills_by_state, aes(x = reorder(state, bill_count), y = bill_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1f78b4") +
  geom_text(aes(label = bill_count), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 States by 2026 Anti-LGBTQ+ Bills Tracked",
    subtitle = "Source: ACLU Legislative Tracker",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Bills"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.callout-note title="Summary"}

This graph shows how Oklahoma leads in the most anti-LGBTQ legislation, followed by West Virginia, Missouri, and more. Minnesota is also on this list, which was surprising for me.

:::

### Viz 3

::: {.callout-note title="Research Question"}

What does anti-LGBTQ legislation for 2026 look like on a map?

:::

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(usmap)

bills_by_state <- legislation_data %>%
  rename(state = State) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(bill_count = n(), .groups = "drop")

plot_usmap(data = bills_by_state, values = "bill_count", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#deebf7",
    high = "#08519c",
    na.value = "grey92",
    name = "Number of Bills"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Anti-LGBTQ+ Bills Tracked by State",
    subtitle = "Source: ACLU Legislative Tracker"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey30")
  )
```
::: {.callout-note title="Summary"}

This map visualizes the same data from viz one, but it is much more effective because it shows the amount of bills in a shaded choropleth. It is much easier to see the data this way.

:::
